extracted.intended_audience: general readers, media professionals, and researchers interested in BBC controversies and editorial/journalistic standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria implied or referenced in a Wikipedia article listing BBC controversies — i.e., editorial, legal, ethical and procedural expectations for broadcast journalism and public-service broadcasting. Covers accuracy, impartiality, contributor handling, complaints, privacy, diversity, and governance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of telephone competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions must be conducted fairly; technical problems that result in rigging (e.g. with receiving calls) are unacceptable and broadcasters have been fined for faking telephone competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure call-in systems work correctly; do not manipulate results; maintain trust in audience-facing competitions; failures may lead to fines and reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of anti-competitive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using public-service resources to undermine commercial suppliers (e.g. BBC Jam accused of providing a free service that competed with commercial educational software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When launching publicly funded services, consider impact on commercial markets; suspend or review services if credible complaints of anti-competitive behaviour arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate editing and representation of subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing must not misrepresent the order or meaning of events (e.g. trailer edits that made the Queen appear to leave a shoot abruptly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not edit shots out of sequence to create false impressions; maintain checks to prevent misleading sequencing; misrepresentation can require formal apology and lead to resignations and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for audience participation and vote integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewer votes and interactive audience inputs must be respected and not altered (e.g. Blue Peter producers changing an internet vote result breached audience trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve transparency of voting processes; if errors occur, disclose and apologise to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding broadcast of harassing or offensive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not broadcast content that harasses, humiliates, or sexually denigrates individuals (e.g. Russell Brand/Jonathan Ross prank calls causing complaints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legality, consent and potential harm before airing prank or intrusive material; be prepared to respond to complaints and take disciplinary action where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality in appeals and news coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid actions that could compromise or be perceived to compromise the BBC's impartiality (e.g. refusal to broadcast DEC Gaza appeal cited risk to impartiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance impartiality concerns with public interest and humanitarian considerations; consider consensus with other broadcasters; transparently justify decisions to avoid perceptions of partisanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of journalistic independence and staff freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be free to speak and not be threatened with dismissal for expressing disagreement about editorial decisions (complaints that journalists were threatened over the DEC decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect internal dissent and whistleblowing; avoid punitive measures that suppress legitimate journalistic debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of sources and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant claims must be corroborated and not rely unquestioningly on single or dubious sources (e.g. reports based heavily on an unchallenged CIA report led to false claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question and cross-check source material; insufficient verification can lead to apologies, corrections, and loss of credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt apologies and correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: When mistakes are made (e.g. false child labour footage, inaccurate reports), the BBC issues apologies and sometimes formal investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue timely, clear apologies and corrections; conduct internal review; accept responsibility where appropriate to restore public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sensationalism and one-sided reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must avoid sensationalism and undue bias; programmes criticised for being one-sided, sensationalist or unethical (e.g. Panorama's Euro 2012 piece).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present balanced coverage, include dissenting voices, avoid cherry-picking or manipulating sources to fit a thesis; unethical presentation can damage subjects and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity and avoidance of racist/xenophobic remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenters should avoid derogatory, stereotyped or racist comments (e.g. Top Gear remarks about Mexicans) which cause complaints and diplomatic protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of international and cultural context; issue apologies and corrective action when remarks cause offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust child-protection policy and investigation of abuse allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of child abuse must be investigated properly and not shelved (e.g. Newsnight investigation into Jimmy Savile was shelved then criticised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and enforce strong child-protection procedures; investigate allegations promptly; failures can trigger inquiries and resignations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify contributors of substantive changes to programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors should be informed when programme content changes significantly from the original commission (e.g. Secret World of Lewis Carroll contributors were not given notice of new controversial material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform contributors early about major changes and give adequate time to consider and respond; failing to do so can breach codes of conduct and require reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate tone and preparation for major events
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage style should suit the occasion (e.g. Diamond Jubilee coverage was criticised for being too informal/lowbrow for a royal event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure presenters are prepared to add historical/contextual depth and match the expected tone of significant public occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of ageism and sexism in staffing and programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring and programme decisions must not discriminate by age or sex (e.g. dismissals of older female presenters and policies to force women onto panels prompted debate about tokenism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote diversity genuinely (avoid tokenism); ensure employment decisions are non-discriminatory and justifiable; monitor outcomes and address bias claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about staging or coordination of broadcast events
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid presenting pre-arranged or coordinated events as spontaneous news (e.g. Daily Politics coordinating an on-air resignation to create drama).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about staging; do not mislead viewers about spontaneity or manipulate timing for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability in executive pay and severance
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior executive payoffs and severance should be justified and transparent to licence-payers; excessive payments prompted public and parliamentary criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish and explain senior payments; consider caps on severance to avoid public outrage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for privacy and legal guidelines during policing coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of police operations (e.g. property searches) must respect strict legal/guideline limits and individuals' privacy rights; unlawful or collusive leaking to media can lead to legal action and damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow police-media guidelines, weigh public interest against privacy, and avoid collaboration that could be construed as extortion or unlawful disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust complaints handling and internal review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: When high volumes of complaints occur (e.g. tens of thousands over an appeal decision), the organisation and regulator (BBC Trust, Ofcom) must review and respond appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear complaint channels, document responses, conduct independent reviews when significant controversies arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not edit or omit sources simply because they contradict a thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not exclude or cut interviews because they fail to confirm a pre-formed thesis (accusations that Panorama omitted an interview that didn't confirm its anti-semitism thesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and fairly present contradictory evidence; manipulate editing to fit a thesis undermines credibility and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in political coverage (airtime, sequencing, source presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Political coverage should be fair in allocation of airtime, ordering of items, prevalence of negative content, and accurately label sources as impartial or partisan (e.g. monitoring found bias against 'Yes' campaign in Scottish referendum coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and correct for bias in airtime and sequencing; present sources transparently and avoid misleading presentations that imply impartiality where it does not exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary transparency and addressing pay gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish disclosures of high earners and address gender and ethnic pay disparities (e.g. publication of employees earning >£150,000 revealed gender imbalance and prompted pay changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparency to identify and remediate pay inequality; be prepared to act on disparities (reassignments, pay cuts, resignations may follow).
